text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A series of bomb blasts hit Jizzine. Four people killed and two wounded.
- Latest government economic measures for reconsideration at cabinet session.
- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir: Lebanon provides good opportunities for investment and trade.
- Phonetapping to be investigated by a new committee.
- Israeli warplanes strike into the outskirts of Mashgara, in the southwestern area of the Bekaa Valley.
- Banque Audi shares push market indexes up.
- Cabinet refuses to reconsider decisions to raise custom duties on imported cars and luxury food items.
- Lebanon's chambers of commerce demand the government to reconsider its economic decisions saying they threatened to the country's liberal economic system.
- Five Malaysian companies bought from Solidere 8,000 square metres of land in central Beirut for a $75 million tourism development.
